issues.legal_issue: A proposed plaint amendment should be permitted where the suit remains at the pre-trial stage, the amendment does not change the nature of the suit, and the procedural history explains why the application was made when it was.
material_facts: The suit had initially been dismissed as not maintainable before trial and was later remanded for decision on the merits.
After remand, the plaintiff applied to amend the plaint; the trial had not begun.
The proposed amendment did not change the nature of the suit.
issues.conclusion: The application to amend the plaint should have been allowed, subject to payment of costs; the defendant was to have an opportunity to make consequential amendments to its written statement.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the Court considered that the suit was still at its initial stage, the proposed amendment did not change the nature of the suit, and the procedural history meant the application could not be treated as belated. In those circumstances, the courts should have taken a liberal approach. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: application_to_amend_in_pending_suit and suit_at_pretrial_stage and amendment_preserves_suit_nature and application_follows_remand_after_earlier_maintainability_dismissal

predicates.application_to_amend_in_pending_suit: A party to a pending civil suit applied to amend its pleading.
predicates.suit_at_pretrial_stage: The suit had not yet reached trial.
predicates.amendment_preserves_suit_nature: The proposed amendment did not change the nature of the suit.
predicates.application_follows_remand_after_earlier: The suit had been dismissed as not maintainable before trial, remanded for trial, and the amendment application was made after remand.

issues.definition: When an amendment application in a pending suit is made before trial, preserves the nature of the suit, and follows remand after an earlier pre-trial dismissal on maintainability grounds, the amendment is allowed on terms.

issues.legal_issue: Additional documents should be permitted to be filed in a pending suit that remains at the pre-trial stage where the documents are alleged to be the opposing party’s documents and were obtained through an information request.
material_facts: The suit had been remanded for trial after its earlier dismissal as not maintainable.
The plaintiff applied after remand to file additional documents, before trial had begun.
The plaintiff alleged that the documents belonged to the defendants and had obtained them through an information request.
issues.conclusion: The application to file the additional documents should have been allowed, subject to payment of costs; the defendants were given an opportunity to file rebuttal documents.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 7 Rule 14 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the Court applied the same grounds as for the amendment application: the suit was at its initial stage and trial had not begun. It also noted that the documents were alleged to be the defendants’ own documents and had been obtained through an information request. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.application_to_file_documents_in_pending: A party to a pending civil suit applied to file additional documents.
predicates.suit_at_pretrial_stage: The suit had not yet reached trial.
predicates.documents_allegedly_belong_to_opposing_p: The filing party alleged that the documents belonged to the opposing party.
predicates.documents_obtained_through_information_r: The filing party obtained the documents through an information request.

issues.definition: When a party applies to file additional documents before trial in a pending suit, and the documents are alleged to belong to the opposing party and were obtained through an information request, the documents are allowed to be filed on terms.

issues.legal_issue: The rejection of an application seeking an order for the opposing party to produce original documents should stand where no argument is advanced against that rejection on appeal.
material_facts: The plaintiff had applied for a direction requiring the defendants to produce original documents.
The trial court and the High Court rejected that application.
The plaintiff’s counsel advanced no argument on the application before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The rejection of the application for production of documents was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The Court upheld the rejection because no argument was advanced on the application. The judgment cites no specific provision or earlier case as the basis for this ruling.

predicates.appeal_from_rejection_of_document_produc: A party appealed an order rejecting a request for the opposing party to produce documents.
predicates.lower_courts_rejected_request: The lower courts rejected the request for production.
predicates.appellant_advanced_no_argument_on_reques: The appellant advanced no argument on the production request in the appeal.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges the rejection of a document-production request, the lower courts rejected it, and the appellant advances no argument on it, the rejection is upheld.
